section_summary.extract_value: This section reports preliminary analyses: Little's MCAR indicated missing data were completely at random and mean replacement was used; descriptive statistics are reported in Table 1. Independent-samples t-tests with a Bonferroni-corrected alpha (p = .004) found only three significant sex differences (women higher on pressure to conform to media-driven appearance ideals, appearance attention, and appearance-management behaviours; men higher on internalisation of a muscular/athletic ideal), and subsequent analyses were conducted separately by sex. No study label (e.g., 'Study 1') or sample size, demographic percentages, assessment methods, BMI values, or correlations between body appreciation and BMI are reported in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: "Based on Little's MCAR analyses, missing data were completely at random, so we used the mean replacement technique to estimate missing values." "Descriptive statistics (M and SD) for all variables are reported in Table 1." "Of the comparisons, only three reached significance (see Table 1): women compared to men reported significantly higher pressure to conform to media-driven appearance ideals and were significantly more likely to attend to their appearance and engaged in appearance-management behaviours; men, on the other hand, were significantly more likely than women to report internalisation of a muscular or athletic appearance ideal." "we nevertheless conducted all subsequent analyses separately by sex because of the possibility of sex-specific effects (Swami, Ng, et al., 2016)."
